name: Berkeley
authority: City of Berkeley household sorting guide. Each household has a blue recycling bin, a green compost bin, and a grey trash bin. For 1-9 unit buildings the Ecology Center supplies the recycling carts. The city's dark-blue recycling cart is for 10 or more units and is not used here.

cardboard_box.reason: Flatten clean cardboard; bundle oversized pieces beside the cart.

also.quote: If you have too much cardboard to fit into your container, flatten and tie up to one 1 foot x 2 feet x 3 feet bundle and place next to your cart.

pizza_box_greasy.reason: Greasy pizza boxes go in the green compost cart.
pizza_box_greasy.quote: Food-soiled paper, such as pizza boxes

paper_mixed.reason: Clean paper and mail go in the blue recycling cart.

paperboard_box.note: Clean dry paper and cardboard are recycling. Cereal and cracker boxes are not named.

paper_bag.note: Clean dry paper is recycling. Paper bags are not named.

shredded_paper.note: Clean dry paper is recycling. Shredded paper is not named.

paper_towel_napkin.note: Uncoated napkins are compost. Paper towels are kept out of paper recycling and are not in the compost list.

tissue.note: Not named. Paper towels are kept out of recycling. Napkins are compost. Facial tissue is neither.

paper_cup.note: Only BPI-certified compostable cups are sent to compost. A plain paper coffee cup is not given a bin.

paper_plate_used.note: Compost accepts uncoated paper plates. The guide does not say every used paper plate.

paper_takeout.reason: Food-soiled paper take-out boxes go in the green cart.
paper_takeout.quote: Food-soiled paper, such as pizza boxes

carton.reason: Milk and juice cartons go in the gray cart.

aseptic_carton.reason: Juice and soup cartons go in the gray cart.

receipt.note: Not named. Clean dry paper is recycling. Thermal receipts are not named.

coffee_grounds_filter.note: Coffee grounds are compost. Paper filters are not named, so the combined item is not settled.

tea_bag.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

book.note: Not named. Clean dry paper is recycling. Books are not named.

plastic_bottle.reason: Empty plastic bottles go in the blue cart.

plastic_jug.reason: Empty plastic jugs go in the blue cart.

plastic_tub.reason: Empty, scraped plastic tubs go in recycling.

plastic_clamshell.reason: Plastic containers go in recycling; empty and clean.

plastic_cup.reason: Plastic cups go in the gray landfill cart.
plastic_cup.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

plastic_takeout.reason: Plastic containers go in recycling; empty and clean.

plastic_bag.reason: Plastic bags and film go in the gray cart.
plastic_bag.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

bubble_wrap.reason: Plastic film goes in the gray landfill cart.
bubble_wrap.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

plastic_utensils.reason: Plastic utensils go in the landfill cart.
plastic_utensils.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

straw.reason: Straws go in the landfill cart.
straw.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

snack_wrapper.reason: Chip bags and wrappers go in the landfill cart.
snack_wrapper.quote: Plastic bags, cups, utensils, straws and films

compostable_plastic.note: BPI-certified compostable paper is compost. Compostable plastic is not named.

foam_food_container.reason: Foam and polystyrene go in the landfill cart.

foam_packaging.reason: Foam and polystyrene go in the landfill cart.

plastic_cap.reason: Small plastic lids go in the gray cart.
plastic_cap.quote: Small plastics, such as lids and utensils (put in landfill container)

coffee_pod.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

drink_pouch.note: Not named. Plastic bags and film are landfill. Drink pouches are not named.

toothpaste_tube.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

toothbrush.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

plastic_toy.note: Not named. Rigid plastic containers are recycling. Toys are not named.

aluminum_can.reason: Empty aluminum cans go in the blue cart.

food_can.reason: Empty, scraped metal cans go in recycling.

aluminum_foil.reason: Clean foil goes in the blue cart.

aluminum_tray.note: Cans and foil are recycling. Trays are not named.

aerosol_can.note: Not named. Cans are recycling. Aerosol cans are not named.

glass_bottle.reason: Empty glass bottles go in the blue cart.

glass_jar.reason: Empty, scraped glass jars go in recycling.

broken_glass.note: Not named. Dishware and window glass are sent to the Transfer Station in one list and to landfill in another.

drinking_glass.note: Dishware and window glass are sent to the Transfer Station in one list and to landfill in another.

ceramic.note: Ceramics are sent to the Transfer Station in one list and to landfill in another.

food_scraps.reason: Food scraps go in the green compost cart.

food_in_container.reason: Scrape the food into the compost cart first, then scan the empty container.

also.quote: Liquids or food (food scraps can be put in compost container)

bones.note: Food scraps are compost. Meat and bones are not named.

yard_trimmings.reason: Branches and leaves go in the green cart.
yard_trimmings.quote: Plant and yard debris, such as branches and leaves (tree branches should be no more than 2 feet in length and no more than 2 inches in diameter if placed in compost container. Lid must close down completely with no obstructions).

flowers.note: Plant and yard debris, such as branches and leaves, is compost. Flowers are not named.

cooking_oil.note: Not named. The guide sends some liquids to container recycling and does not name cooking oil.

wooden_chopsticks.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

battery.reason: Batteries cannot go in the carts; see stopwaste.org/hhw.
battery.quote: Household hazardous waste like batteries, fertilizers, pesticides, chemicals, paints and electronics cannot be disposed in your curbside carts.

also.quote: For proper disposal options contact (800) 606-6606 or visit stopwaste.org/hhw.

phone_electronics.reason: Electronics cannot go in the carts; see stopwaste.org/hhw.

cords_cables.note: Electronics are kept out of the carts. Cords and cables are not named.

bulb_fluorescent.note: Hazardous waste is kept out of the carts. Fluorescent bulbs are not named.

bulb_led.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

bulb_incandescent.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

paint.reason: Paint cannot go in the carts; see stopwaste.org/hhw.
paint.quote: Household hazardous waste like batteries, fertilizers, pesticides, chemicals, paints and electronics cannot be disposed in your curbside carts.

also.quote: For proper disposal options contact (800) 606-6606 or visit stopwaste.org/hhw.

cleaning_product.quote: Household hazardous waste like batteries, fertilizers, pesticides, chemicals, paints and electronics cannot be disposed in your curbside carts.

medicine.note: Not named. The hazardous-waste sentence names chemicals, paints, and electronics, not medicine.

sharps.note: Not named on the household sorting guide or the 1-9 unit hazardous-waste sentence.

propane_cylinder.note: Not named on the household sorting guide or the 1-9 unit hazardous-waste sentence.

diaper.reason: Diapers go in the landfill cart.

pet_waste.reason: Pet waste goes in the landfill cart.

kitty_litter.note: Pet waste is landfill. Cat litter is not named.

face_mask.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

disposable_gloves.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

textiles.note: Not named. Furniture can be donated. Clothing is not named.

shoes.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

cigarette.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

wipes.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

garden_hose.note: Not named on the household sorting guide.

egg_carton_paper.reason: Paper egg cartons go in the blue cart.

egg_carton_foam.reason: Foam and polystyrene go in the landfill cart.

frozen_food_box.note: The gray bin mentions lined paper food cartons. Frozen food boxes are not named.
